title: 5.2.3 Lab: A random spot and colour
description: Once a second, move a coin to a random place, roll a whole-number die, and give the coin a random colour from a list.

steps.title: A random spot
steps.instructions: `draw()` already has a block that runs once a second: `if (frameCount % 60 === 0) { ... }`. Inside it, set `coin.x` to a random number from 30 to 370 and `coin.y` to a random number from 30 to 270. Run it and wait: once a second the coin should jump to a new place, always fully on the canvas.
hints: `random(min, max)` gives a number from `min` up to `max`. Decimals are fine for a position.
`coin.x = random(30, 370);` is one of the two lines. The other one is for `coin.y`.

steps.title: Roll a die
steps.instructions: Inside the same block, set `roll` to a random whole number from 1 to 6. The number shows in the top corner. Watch a dozen rolls and check that you see a 6 and never a 0 or a 7.
hints: `random` gives decimals, and `floor` cuts them off. Wrap one in the other.
The top number is never reached, so for 1 to 6 write `floor(random(1, 7))`. `floor(random(6)) + 1` also works.

steps.title: A random colour
steps.instructions: Inside the same block, pick a random position in the `colors` list: a whole number from 0 up to the last position. Then set `coin.color` to the colour at that position. Use the list's `.length` so the line keeps working if a colour is added.
hints: `colors.length` is how many colours there are. Five colours means the positions are 0 to 4.
`const pick = floor(random(colors.length));` gives the position, and `colors[pick]` reads the colour there.

requirements.title: The coin gets a random x
requirements.description: The x position comes from random(...). Help: 5.2.1 (Reading: Random numbers and timers)

requirements.title: The coin gets a random y
requirements.description: The y position comes from random(...). Help: 5.2.1 (Reading: Random numbers and timers)

requirements.title: The die is a whole number from 1 to 6
requirements.description: random is wrapped in floor and shifted so the answers run 1 to 6. Help: 5.2.1 (Reading: Random numbers and timers)
requirements.hint: The top of random(1, 7) is never reached, so floor of it is 1 to 6.

requirements.title: A random position in the colors list
requirements.description: A whole number from 0 to the list's last position is chosen at random, using the list's length. Help: 5.2.1 (Reading: Random numbers and timers)
requirements.hint: floor(random(colors.length)) is a whole number from 0 to 4.

requirements.title: The coin takes the chosen colour
requirements.description: coin.color is set from the colors list. Help: 5.2.1 (Reading: Random numbers and timers)
requirements.hint: colors[pick] reads the colour at that position. Assign it to coin.color.
